settings.title: 01 USB-C power & amp-draw check

settings.title: 02 Microscope corrosion trace

settings.question: My MacBook still turns on after a spill. Do I still need a liquid damage inspection?
settings.answer: Yes. Liquid leaves conductive mineral residue under microchips and connectors that continues to corrode silently over days or weeks. Switching the MacBook off now and booking an ultrasonic clean and inspection stops a minor spill from turning into a major power-rail short.

settings.question: Will my data be safe during a MacBook liquid damage repair?
settings.answer: Because modern MacBook Air and MacBook Pro SSDs are soldered directly to the logic board, repairing your original logic board is the best way to keep your files intact. Liquid damage can be unpredictable and there is a small chance data could be affected if the storage circuit itself was damaged, so during diagnostics we prioritise protecting your data wherever possible.

settings.question: Should I put my wet MacBook in rice or use a hairdryer?
settings.answer: No. Neither dries liquid trapped beneath tightly sealed logic board chips. Rice introduces starch dust into fans and ports, and a hairdryer can warp keys, damage display polarisers, and drive liquid deeper into connectors. Power the MacBook off immediately and keep it unplugged.
